data.heading: A before and after, straight from the guide
data.before: “Write an announcement about the office move.”
data.after: “Write an announcement for our staff that we’re moving offices on 3 March. Some people are worried about the commute, so keep the tone warm and calm. Make it an email with a subject line, under 150 words. Include the new address and say that parking details will follow next week. Don’t make any promises about desk assignments, because those aren’t decided yet.”

paras: You ask AI for something, and what comes back is too long, too stiff or beside the point. So you correct it, and correct it again. Free plans cap how much you can send, so every correction costs you.
This guide gives you twelve habits for getting a usable answer with less back-and-forth.

It is for people on the free or basic plans of everyday chat apps who aren’t sure AI is worth their time yet. It is also for anyone who has been asked to use more AI at work. You don’t need a paid plan, and you don’t need to code.

items.name: Give each job its own chat.
Paste the real thing instead of describing it.
Check its work before your name goes on it.

data.heading: A sample page
data.first_alt: Guide page 6 of 22, where Part 3 begins. Commandment 1, Give each job its own chat: the rule in one line, why it works, a before-and-after example for work (a sales rep and a thank-you note) and one for everyday life (a birthday dinner chat and a letter to an insurer), and where to find the setting in your app.
data.second_alt: Guide page 7 of 22. The end of Commandment 1 with its 10-second check, then Commandment 2, Choose your prompt: plan, make or check, with three starter sentences to copy and before-and-after examples for work and for a trip plan.

items.name: Why it works, in plain words.
A before-and-after example from work and from home.
Where to find the setting in your app.
A short test to run before you hit send.
Three kinds of request: plan, make and check. The guide shows you how to keep them apart.
Two fill-in sheets you can copy and paste, so the AI knows who you are and writes in your voice.
A one-page card with all twelve, to print or keep by your screen.

items.name: What Not to Put Into AI
items.detail: Covers what should never go into an AI chat, such as private, client or company information.
